2026-09-27 observation 2 of 2 Google AI Overview · incognito, signed out · paste evidence · 8 sources · PER 0.75
PHASE X READ AS 'PHASES': at 'phase x marx', where in June the same surface defined Phase X and named Johannes Sigil, the Overview answers with the two phases of communism from the Gotha Programme. It misquotes the Soviet formula 'to each according to his work' as Marx's, and keeps Phase X only as an unlinked 'Further Exploration' line beside #843's card.
Reading

In June this string composed as a definition: Phase X as a reconstruction of 'a perceived missing transition' in Marx's early writings, with Johannes Sigil named as its commentator and Zenodo cited on every claim. Now 'phase x' is read as 'phases' and answered with the two phases of communism from the Critique of the Gotha Programme, lower and higher. Each phase is filled into the same four-slot template, and the template produces one misattribution and one mislabel. (1) The lower phase's 'Distribution Principle' is given as a quotation, 'From each according to his ability, to each according to his work.' That formula is not in the Gotha text. It is the Soviet socialist principle, fixed in Article 12 of the 1936 Constitution. Marx describes a labour certificate that returns to the worker what the worker gave, after deductions. (2) The higher phase's 'Limitations' slot lists the withering of the state and the end of class and exploitation. Those are its achievements, not limits; the slot was filled because the template required it. The 'birthmarks' line is Marx's. Phase X survives as one line under 'Further Exploration', 'a philological analysis of the missing manuscript transition regarding alienation from Phase X', with no link and no author. #843's maryleelabor page sits fourth in a rail of stage-theory sources.

Machine text, verbatim
AI Mode Conversation You said: phase x marx Karl Marx described the development of communist society in his 1875 work Critique of the Gotha Programme [link] as having two distinct phases (often referred to by later theorists like Lenin as socialism and communism): [1, 2, 3] The First (Lower) Phase of Communism * Definition: The transitional society that directly emerges after the overthrow of capitalism (during the dictatorship of the proletariat). [1, 2] * Economic Basis: Society still bears the "birthmarks" of the old capitalist society from which it emerged. [1] * Distribution Principle: "From each according to his ability, to each according to his work." Individuals are compensated based on the amount and contribution of labor they provide. [1] * Limitations: Social classes are disappearing, but economic inequality, legal rights tied to labor output, and remnants of the state apparatus still persist. [1] The Higher Phase of Communism * Definition: The fully developed, mature classless society. [1] * Economic Basis: The productive forces have massively increased, and the enslaving subordination of individuals to the division of labor has vanished. [1] * Distribution Principle: "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs." Goods and resources are abundantly available for all citizens regardless of how much labor they perform. [1] * Limitations: The state has completely "withered away," and class distinctions, commodity production, and exploitation are entirely gone. [1, 2] Further Exploration * Explore a philological analysis of the missing manuscript transition regarding alienation from Phase X. * Review historical materialist development through Dialectical Historicism [link]. [1, 2] [source card 1] Liga Internacional de los Trabajadores — "
